Surah al-Fath (The Victory) — Medinan, revealed on the way back from al-Hudaybiyah, and its verses number 29.

﴿Indeed We have given you a clear victory﴾: We decreed the conquest of Makkah and others in the future, by force, through your striving (jihad), ﴿a clear victory﴾, evident and manifest.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 48, verse 2:

﴿That Allah may forgive you your sins, past and future﴾ through your jihad, ﴿that﴾ is, the sins committed by you, ﴿so that He may encourage your community to engage in jihad. And it is interpreted as referring to the infallibility (ʿiṣmah) of the prophets, peace be upon them, by the decisive rational proof that they are free from sins. The lam here indicates the final cause (ʿillah ghāʾiyyah), so what follows it is an effect, not a cause.﴾ ﴿And He may complete His favour﴾ by the aforementioned victory, ﴿His blessing﴾, His bestowal ﴿upon you, and guide you﴾ through it ﴿to a path﴾, a way, ﴿straight﴾, one by which He keeps you firm, ﴿which is the religion of Islam﴾.
﴿And Allah will help you⦗with⦘ a mighty help⦗, one of might, with no humiliation in it⦘.

He it is who sent down tranquility (al-sakinah, i.e. serenity) into the hearts of the believers, that they might increase in faith along with their faith, [i.e., with the legal rulings of the religion, each time one of them was revealed they believed in it, and among them was jihad]. And to Allah belong the armies of the heavens and the earth; had He willed to support His religion without you, He would have done so. And Allah is ever Knowing of His creation, Wise in His creation, i.e., He has never ceased to be characterized by that.
﴿That He may admit﴾ is مُتَعَلِّق بِمَحْذُوفٍ (mutaʿallaq bi-mahdhūf), meaning it is grammatically dependent on an omitted element. That is, He commanded jihad (striving in the way of God).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 48, verse 6:

﴿And He will punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and polytheist women, who assume about Allah an assumption of evil.﴾ [The word] "al-saw'" is read with a fatha and with a damma on the sin in the three places [in this verse and the two that follow]. They thought that He would not give victory to Muhammad (ﷺ) and the believers. ﴿Upon them is a circle of evil.﴾ [That is], with humiliation and punishment. ﴿And Allah has become angry with them and has cursed them﴾ [meaning] He has removed them [far from His mercy]. ﴿And He has prepared for them Hell, and evil is it as a destination﴾ [meaning] a place of return.
"And to Allah belongs the hosts of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is ever Mighty" in His dominion, "Wise" in His creation, meaning He has always been characterized by that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 48, verse 8:

﴿Indeed, We have sent you as a witness﴾ over your ummah on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿and a bringer of good tidings﴾ to them in the world, ﴿and a warner﴾ warning and frightening them in it of the Fire for whoever does evil.

﴿That you may believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾, with the verb read with the yāʾ (يُؤْمِنُوا, the third-person form) and with the tāʾ (تُؤْمِنُوا, the second-person form), both in this word and in the three verbs that follow it. ﴿And support him﴾ (ويُعَزِّرُوهُ), meaning yanṣurūhu (help him). It is also read with two zāy's (تُعَزِّزُوهُ), together with the reading using the upper tāʾ (fawqāniyya, the tāʾ with the dot above it, i.e., the second-person form). ﴿And honour him﴾ (ويُوَقِّرُوهُ), meaning yuʿaẓẓimūhu (revere and exalt him). Its pronoun refers either to Allah or to His Messenger. ﴿And glorify Him﴾ (ويُسَبِّحُوهُ), meaning Allah. ﴿Morning and evening﴾ (بُكْرَة وأَصِيلًا), meaning at dawn and in the afternoon.

﴿Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you﴾ at al-Hudaybiyya, in the Pledge of Ridwan (Bay'at al-Ridwan), ﴿indeed they pledge allegiance only to God﴾. This is like ﴿whoever obeys the Messenger has indeed obeyed God﴾. ﴿The hand of God is above their hands﴾, which they used to pledge allegiance to the Prophet. That is, He, exalted is He, is aware of their pledge and will reward them for it. ﴿Whoever breaks [the pledge]﴾ means he annuls the pledge, ﴿then he breaks only against himself﴾, meaning the harm of his breaking returns to himself. ﴿And whoever fulfills what he covenanted with God, He will give him﴾, with the verb read with the letter yā' (بِالياءِ), "He will give him," and with the letter nūn (والنُّون), "We will give him."

﴿The ones left behind among the Bedouin will say to you﴾ around Madinah, namely those whom Allah kept from accompanying you when I called them to go out with you to Makkah, out of fear that Quraysh would confront you in the year of al-Hudaybiyyah if you returned from it. ﴿Our wealth and our families have occupied us﴾ from going out with you. ﴿So ask forgiveness for us﴾ from Allah for leaving off going out with you. Allah the Exalted said, refuting them: ﴿They say with their tongues﴾ that is, when asking for forgiveness and what preceded it, ﴿what is not in their hearts.﴾ So they are liars in their excuse. ﴿Say: Who then﴾ is an istifham (interrogative) that carries the meaning of negation, meaning no one ﴿can control anything for you from Allah if He intends harm for you﴾ with the ḍād of ﴿ضَرًّا﴾ pronounced with a fatḥah or a ḍammah, ﴿or intends benefit for you? Rather, Allah is ever, of what you do, Ever-Aware.﴾ That is, He has never ceased to be characterized by that.

﴿Bal﴾ (rather/nay, but) in both places is for moving from one topic to another. ﴿You thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families again, and that this was made attractive in your hearts﴾, meaning: they would be wiped out by killing, so they would not come back. ﴿And you harboured an evil assumption﴾, this and other such thoughts. ﴿And you were a people ruined﴾; the word is the plural of bā'ir (ruined, lost), meaning: destroyed in the sight of God because of this assumption.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 48, verse 13:

﴿And whoever does not believe in Allah and His Messenger – then indeed We have prepared for the disbelievers a blaze﴾ — a fierce fire.

﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful﴾. That is, He has never ceased to be characterized by what has been mentioned.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 48, verse 15:

﴿Those who were left behind will say﴾, those mentioned, ﴿when you set out to take spoils﴾, which are the spoils of Khaybar, ﴿to take them, "Let us follow you."﴾ Leave us (﴿Let us follow you﴾) so that we may take some of them. ﴿They want﴾ by that ﴿to change the words of Allah.﴾ And in another reading: kalim Allah, with the lam kasra (i.e., His promises), with the spoils of Khaybar being for the people of al-Hudaybiyya specifically. ﴿Say, "You will never follow us; thus has Allah said before"﴾, i.e., before our return. ﴿So they will say, "Rather, you envy us."﴾ That we would obtain some of the spoils with you, so you said that. ﴿Rather, they did not understand﴾ of the religion ﴿except a little﴾ of them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 48, verse 16:

﴿Say to the desert Arabs who were left behind⟩ those mentioned, being tested, ﴿"You will be called to a people of⟩ possessors of ﴿great might⟩. It was said they are the Banu Hanifa, the people of al-Yamama; and it was said they are Persia and the Romans. ﴿You will fight them⟩ a anticipated circumstance (hal muqaddara), which is the one they are called to in meaning. ﴿Or⟩ they ﴿will submit⟩, so you will not fight. ﴿If you obey⟩ in fighting them, ﴿Allah will give you a good reward, but if you turn away as you turned away before, He will punish you with a painful punishment⟩ causing pain.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 48, verse 17:

﴿There is no blame on the blind, nor is there blame on the lame, nor is there blame on the sick﴾ for abstaining from jihad. ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, He will admit him﴾ (with the ya' and the nun, i.e., yudkhiluhu or nudkhiluhu) ﴿to gardens beneath which rivers flow. And whoever turns away, He will punish him﴾ (with the ya' and the nun, i.e., yu'adhdhibhu or nu'adhdhibhu).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 48, verse 18:

﴿Indeed, Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you﴾ at al-Hudaybiyah, ﴿under the tree﴾, which was a samurah tree, and they were one thousand three hundred or more. Then he (ﷺ) took their pledge that they would fight the Quraysh and that they would not flee from death. ﴿So He knew﴾ (Allah) ﴿what was in their hearts﴾ of truthfulness and loyalty, ﴿and He sent down tranquility upon them and rewarded them with an imminent victory﴾, which was the conquest of Khaybar after their return from al-Hudaybiyah.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 48, verse 19:

﴿And much booty that they will take﴾ from Khaybar. ﴿And ever is Allah Almighty, All-Wise﴾, i.e., He has never ceased to be characterized by that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 48, verse 20:

﴿And Allah promised you much booty that you will take﴾ from the conquests, ﴿and He hastened this for you﴾ the spoils of Khaybar, ﴿and restrained the hands of the people from you﴾ regarding your families when you went out, and the Jews intended against them, so Allah cast terror into their hearts. ﴿And that it may be a sign for the believers﴾ i.e., the hastened spoil, conjoined to a implied clause, meaning: so that you may thank Him, ﴿and that He may guide you to a straight path﴾ i.e., the way of trusting in Him and entrusting the matter to Him, exalted is He.

﴿And others﴾ is an attribute (ṣifah) of "spoils" (maghānim), with an implied subject (mubtada', the grammatical subject of a nominal sentence) understood as "it" ﴿you were not able to obtain﴾ ﴿it is from Persia and Rome﴾ ﴿Allah has already encompassed them﴾ He knew that they would be yours ﴿And Allah is ever Capable of everything﴾ i.e., He has always been characterized by that.
﴿And if those who disbelieve had fought you﴾ at al-Hudaybiyah ﴿they would have turned their backs in flight; then they would not find any protector﴾ to guard them.

﴿The way of God﴾ is a verbal noun (maṣdar) emphasizing the meaning of the sentence before it, which concerns the defeat of the disbelievers and the victory of the believers. That is, God established this as a way (sunnah) ﴿that has passed before, and you will never find any change in the way of God﴾ from Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 48, verse 24:

﴿And it is He who withheld their hands from you and your hands from them in the heart of Makkah﴾ at al-Hudaybiyyah, ﴿after He had made you victorious over them.﴾ For eighty of them came down upon your camp, seeking to strike at you; they were seized and brought to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he pardoned them and let them go. That was the cause of the peace treaty. ﴿And Allah is ever Seeing of what you do﴾ — read with the ya' and the ta' (i.e., as both "they do" and "you do"); that is, He has never ceased to be characterized by that.

﴿They are those who disbelieved and barred you from al-Masjid al-Haram (the Sacred Mosque)﴾, i.e., from reaching it. ﴿And the offering﴾ is conjoined (ma'tūf, grammatically coordinated) with the pronoun كم (kum, "you") in the phrase "barred you." ﴿Restrained﴾ (مَعْكُوفًا, ma'kūfan) means detained, and it is in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial qualifier, describing the state of the offering). ﴿From reaching its place﴾ (مَحِلّه, maḥillahu), i.e., the place where it is customarily slaughtered, which is the Haram. This phrase is a badal al-ishtimal (substitution of inclusion, where the substitute is related to the substituted element as a part, quality or containing whole, rather than being identical with it).

﴿And were it not for believing men and believing women﴾ present in Makkah among the disbelievers (lawlā, "were it not for," introduces a conditional whose response is omitted), ﴿whom you did not know to be believers﴾ by their faith, ﴿that you might trample them﴾, i.e., kill them along with the disbelievers, ﴿had you been permitted to conquer﴾. This phrase is a badal al-ishtimal from the pronoun "them" (hum). ﴿A burden would have fallen upon you from them﴾, i.e., sin, ﴿without knowledge﴾ on your part of it. The pronouns of absence (ḍamā'ir al-ghayba) refer to both groups by giving precedence to the masculine (taghlīb al-dhukūr). The jawāb (response, apodosis) of lawlā is omitted, meaning: "you would have been permitted to conquer, but permission was not given at that time."

﴿That Allah may admit into His mercy whom He wills﴾, such as the believers mentioned. ﴿Had they been distinguished﴾, separated from the disbelievers, ﴿We would have punished those of them who disbelieved﴾, from the people of Makkah at that time, by permitting you to conquer it, ﴿with a painful punishment﴾, i.e., one causing pain.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 48, verse 26:

﴿When﴾ relates to ﴿We punished﴾. ﴿Those who disbelieved﴾ is the subject of ﴿placed in their hearts zealotry﴾, meaning arrogance (al-anafah) regarding something, ﴿the zealotry of ignorance﴾ being a substitute (badal) for ﴿zealotry﴾. It was their preventing the Prophet and his Companions from the Sacred Mosque. ﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquillity upon His Messenger and upon the believers﴾, so they made a treaty with them on the condition that they would return the following year, and the believers were not affected by zealotry in the way the disbelievers were, until they fought them. ﴿And He required of them﴾, i.e., of the believers, ﴿the word of piety﴾: "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." It was attributed to piety because it is its cause. ﴿And they were more entitled to it﴾, to the word, than the disbelievers, ﴿and worthy of it﴾, a explanatory conjunction (ʿatf tafsīrī). ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing of all things﴾, i.e., He has never ceased to be characterized by this, and among what He knows, exalted is He, is that they were worthy of it.

﴿Allah had certainly made true for His Messenger the vision, in truth.﴾ The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw in a dream, in the year of Hudaybiyyah and before he set out, that he and his companions would enter Makkah securely, with some shaving their heads and others cutting their hair short. He told his companions of this, and they rejoiced. When they set out with him, the unbelievers barred them at Hudaybiyyah, and they returned. This grieved them, and some of the hypocrites were filled with doubt. This verse was revealed. His words "in truth" (bil-haqq) are either connected to "made true" (sadaqa) or are a circumstantial phrase (hal) modifying "the vision," and what follows it.

﴿You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if Allah wills, securely, with your heads shaved and your hair cut short.﴾ The phrase "if Allah wills" is for seeking blessing (lil-tabarruk). "With your heads shaved" means all of the hair, and "and with your hair cut short" means some of it. These two are circumstantial phrases (hal) of a future kind (muqaddarah). ﴿You will not fear﴾ ever.

﴿So He knew﴾ in the peace treaty ﴿what you did not know﴾ of the benefit in it. ﴿So He made, besides that﴾ i.e., besides the entry, ﴿a near victory﴾. This is the conquest of Khaybar. The vision was fulfilled in the following year.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 48, verse 28:

﴿He it is who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion.﴾ That is, the religion of truth ﴿over all religion﴾, over all the other religions. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as a witness﴾ that you are a messenger with what has been mentioned, as Allah the Exalted said.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 48, verse 29:

﴿Muhammad﴾ is the subject (mubtada') ﴿the Messenger of Allah﴾ is its predicate (khabar). ﴿And those with him﴾, i.e., his companions from among the believers, is a subject whose predicate is ﴿harsh (ashidda') against the disbelievers﴾, meaning stern (ghilaz), not showing them mercy. ﴿Merciful (ruhama') among themselves﴾ is a second predicate, i.e., affectionate and loving to one another, like a parent with a child. ﴿You see them﴾, i.e., you look at them, ﴿bowing (ruka') and prostrating (sujjadan)﴾ are two circumstantial clauses (hal). ﴿Seeking﴾ is a new sentence (musta'naf), they seek ﴿bounty from Allah and pleasure﴾. ﴿Their mark (simahum)﴾ is the subject, ﴿in their faces﴾ is its predicate, and it is a light and whiteness by which they are recognized in the Hereafter, that they prostrated in this world, ﴿from the trace of prostration﴾, which is related to what the predicate is related to, i.e., existing (ka'ina). It is parsed as a circumstantial clause (hal) from its pronoun which has shifted to the predicate. ﴿That﴾, the aforementioned description, ﴿is their example (mathaluhum)﴾, their attribute, is a subject, ﴿in the Torah﴾ is its predicate. ﴿And their example in the Gospel﴾ is a subject whose predicate is ﴿like a seed that sends out its shoot (shat'ahu)﴾, with the ta' vowelled either with sukun or fatha, meaning its offshoots. ﴿Then it strengthens it (fa-azarahu)﴾, with madd or qasr, meaning it strengthens and helps it. ﴿Then it becomes thick (fa-istaghlaza)﴾, meaning it became thick. ﴿Then it stands firm (fa-istawa)﴾, meaning it became strong and upright. ﴿On its stems (suqihi)﴾, its roots, plural of saq. ﴿It pleases the sowers (zurra')﴾, i.e., its sowers, because of its goodness, like the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, for they began in few numbers and weakness, then they multiplied and grew strong in the best of forms. ﴿That He may enrage the disbelievers by them﴾ is related to an omitted element indicated by what precedes it, i.e., they were likened to that. ﴿Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds among them﴾, the Companions; "min" here is explanatory of the genus (li-bayan al-jins), not partitive (li-ltab'id), because they are all characterized by the aforementioned attribute, ﴿forgiveness and a great reward﴾, which is Paradise. These two are also for those who come after them, in verses.
